# SPY Salon – Notification System Audit Report

**Date:** Generated by automated audit workflow  
**Scope:** Flutter mobile app (`mobile_app/`) + Node.js backend (`backend/src/`)

---

## A. Issues Identified

| # | Issue | Severity | File |
|---|-------|----------|------|
| 1 | FCM notification icon used `@mipmap/ic_launcher` (full-colour launcher icon) — Android notification tray requires a monochrome small icon; causes broken/missing icon in system tray on Android 5+ | **HIGH** | `fcm_service.dart`, `AndroidManifest.xml` |
| 2 | `ic_notification.xml` monochrome drawable did not exist | **HIGH** | `android/.../res/drawable/` |
| 3 | `AndroidManifest.xml` missing `com.google.firebase.messaging.default_notification_icon` meta-data — system (background/terminated) FCM notifications used the launcher icon | **HIGH** | `AndroidManifest.xml` |
| 4 | `handleNotificationNavigation()` showed only SnackBars — no actual navigation to a notification screen | **HIGH** | `fcm_service.dart` |
| 5 | `NotificationScreen` did not exist — no dedicated UI to browse, read, and delete notifications | **HIGH** | `notification_screen.dart` (missing) |
| 6 | `ApiService` had no `getNotifications`, `getUnreadNotificationCount`, `markNotificationRead`, `markAllNotificationsRead`, or `deleteNotification` methods | **HIGH** | `api_service.dart` |
| 7 | Neither `CustomerDashboardScreen` nor `EmployeeDashboardScreen` had a notification bell icon or unread badge in the AppBar | **MEDIUM** | `customer_dashboard_screen.dart`, `employee_dashboard_screen.dart` |
| 8 | Dashboards did not listen for `notification:new` / `notifications:updated` Socket.IO events to refresh unread count | **MEDIUM** | both dashboard files |

## D. Firebase Configuration Status

### `google-services.json`
`google-services.json` **exists** at `mobile_app/android/app/google-services.json`. The build is guarded by `if (file("google-services.json").exists())` in `build.gradle.kts` so it compiles without it, but the file is present.

### Backend FCM Environment Variables
The backend `firebaseNotificationService.js` requires the following environment variables (must be set in `.env` or your hosting environment):

```
FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=
FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY=
FIREBASE_CLIENT_EMAIL=
```

These are Firebase Admin SDK credentials. They must be obtained from the Firebase Console → Project Settings → Service Accounts → Generate new private key.

### Firebase Console Requirements
- A Firebase project must exist and be linked to the app's package name (`android/app/build.gradle` `applicationId`)
- `google-services.json` must come from that same Firebase project
- FCM API must be enabled for the project (it is by default)
- For iOS: `GoogleService-Info.plist` must be added to `ios/Runner/` if iOS support is required

---

## E. Complete Notification Flow

```
Backend Event (e.g. appointment booked, leave approved)
  ↓
dispatchNotification() called in controller
  ↓
MongoDB: Notification document saved (Notification.js model)
  ↓
Socket.IO: targeted event emitted (e.g. notification:new → room:customer, room:employee, room:admin)
  ↓
FCM: firebaseNotificationService.sendPushToUser() → Firebase Admin SDK → FCM servers
  ↓
Device receives push notification
  ├── App FOREGROUND: onMessage listener fires → _showForegroundLocalNotification() → flutter_local_notifications banner shown with @drawable/ic_notification
  ├── App BACKGROUND: system tray notification shown with @drawable/ic_notification (via AndroidManifest meta-data); user tap → onMessageOpenedApp fires → handleNotificationNavigation() → NotificationScreen pushed
  └── App TERMINATED: system tray notification shown; user tap → app launches → getInitialMessage() fires after 1200ms delay → handleNotificationNavigation() → NotificationScreen pushed
  ↓
NotificationScreen UI
  ├── Calls ApiService.getNotifications() and getUnreadNotificationCount() on load
  ├── Displays notifications as cards with type icon, title, message, relative time, unread dot
  ├── Tap notification → markNotificationRead() → local state update
  ├── Delete button → deleteNotification() → item removed from list
  └── Mark All Read → markAllNotificationsRead() → full refresh
  ↓
Dashboard AppBar (Customer + Employee)
  └── Bell icon with unread badge updated on: init, return from NotificationScreen, notification:new Socket.IO event
```

## F. Remaining External Requirements

| Item | Owner | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|
| Firebase project creation | Developer | Create at console.firebase.google.com |
| `google-services.json` validity | Developer | Already present; confirm it matches your Firebase project's Android app |
| Firebase Admin SDK credentials | DevOps | Set `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`, `FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY`, `FIREBASE_CLIENT_EMAIL` in backend `.env` |
| iOS `GoogleService-Info.plist` | Developer | Not required for Android-only; needed if iOS is targeted |
| Physical device / emulator testing | QA | Background and terminated state push notification delivery requires a real device or Firebase-capable emulator (not iOS Simulator) |
| Android notification permission | End user | Prompted at runtime on Android 13+ via `requestPermission()` — already implemented |
